BARCELONA, Nov 13 : Spain are set to welcome back forwards Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal for Sunday's Nations League match against England after the duo missed Thursday's 2-0 win over the Czech Republic, manager Luis de la Fuente said. Lamine had stayed back in Barcelona to nurse a knee injury. "Lamine feels very good now and is really looking forward to joining the squad tomorrow," de la Fuente told Spanish television channel La 1. Oyarzabal stayed in San Sebastian to be present at the birth of his second child. De la Fuente confirmed that he would also be part of Spain's Friday evening training session.

Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US-listed maker of cooling systems for data centres, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday (Nov 12), citing people familiar with the matter.  The companies are discussing a potential deal that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the report added. Shares of Modine surged 29 per cent in extended trading following the report. The company had a market value of US$5.6 billion as of Thursday, according to data compiled by LSEG. No final decision has been made and the talks could still fall apart, the report said, adding that another suitor could also emerge. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Samsung and Modine could not be reached for comment immediately.

Source: Reuters/nh

LONDON, Nov 12 : England manager Thomas Tuchel spoke out in support of Ben White after the defender was booed when he came on as a substitute in the 2-1 Nations League win over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday. Tuchel told reporters he had not heard the booing, which contrasted to applause for Croatia's veteran forward Luka Modric as he left the pitch and was widely reported by media present. The Arsenal player was making his first appearance for England since March, before the World Cup which he was not selected for due to injury, and has been booed in the past after turning his back on the national team. He left the 2022 World Cup camp in Qatar early for personal reasons and later made himself unavailable for the remainder of Gareth Southgate’s tenure as England manager, which ended after Euro 2024.

"I didn't hear the boos for Ben and I thought we were past that chapter," said Tuchel after a match that saw captain Harry Kane celebrate his record 126th cap for England with a match-winner from the penalty spot. "I hope it doesn't happen again. He's a player of us. Since I'm in charge he's desperate to come and be with the group. He doesn't put a foot wrong since I'm in charge. "I can only judge him on what I see and what I experienced and it is on the highest level and he can really help us to win football matches," added the German. "Like I said, he's part of our group and we will protect our group. He deserves to be with us." Tuchel said he was not worried White might turn his back on the team if the negative reaction continued. "I don't think so. I don't want to make it bigger than it is," he said. "He seemed to me always committed and always dedicated and excited to come into camp and get a call-up... there is no reason to doubt his commitment or his passion. "He overcame the boos the last time, I didn't hear them this time."

SYDNEY, Nov 13 : Australia captain Pat Cummins again denied any involvement in the plot to use sandpaper on the ball in a test against South Africa in 2018, on Friday describing the allegations in Usman Khawaja's autobiography as "utter nonsense". Former Australia batsman Khawaja, whose autobiography was published on Tuesday, said last weekend that all the players in the team at Newlands knew about the plot, triggering calls for a new investigation into the incident.  "When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," Cummins told a press conference in Sydney. "I did not know that was happening, but I think Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that.

"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense. "There was no master plan around using illegal methods," he added. "There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying 'this is what must happen'." The Australia skipper spoke for 68 minutes, taking every question from the media and saying he would never discuss the ball-tampering incident again. Cummins also took exception to Pakistan-born Khawaja's contention in the book that the colour of his skin and background had prevented him from becoming Australia captain. "I think of all the things that I've read this week, I think that's actually the most serious," he said.  "Him saying that if you're Australian captain, you have to be a certain skin colour, I couldn't disagree with that statement any more." Steve Smith and David Warner, the then Australia captain and vice-captain, were banned by Cricket Australia from elite cricket for a year for their roles in the ball-tampering.  Warner on Monday said he backed Khawaja's version of events as "100 per cent accurate". "There's quite a few different accounts here, so they've got two accounts," said Cummins. "There's 11 players in that room, so that means there's nine other guys who I think it's appropriate you give an equal amount of weighting to their story as well." Opening batter Cameron Bancroft, who brought a piece of sandpaper onto the field, received a nine-month suspension for his part in the ball-tampering. "I was genuinely shocked this week when I found out that Usman admitted that he told Cam to be careful when using sandpaper. That's not the Usman that I know," Cummins said.  "It's not the Usman that has helped rebuild the Australian cricket culture over the last eight years." "CASUAL WITH LIVES AND REPUTATIONS" Cummins was asked about Khawaja's recollection that two players had rejected the batsman's call for the team to take collective responsibility for the ball-tampering. "I don't remember any conversation around collective responsibility," he said. "So then, I've got no idea who those two people would be because I don't remember ever being asked or having a conversation about it." Khawaja and Warner have also been critical of the Cricket Australia investigation in 2018 that found the three punished players solely responsible for the plot. "I got asked to be part of that review," Cummins said. "I was totally truthful. I've been very consistent since then at that event till now. Nothing's changed." Earlier this week,  the head of Cricket Australia ruled out opening another investigation into the 2018 incident. Cummins said he respected the right of Khawaja to tell his story in the autobiography but felt some of the allegations were very serious and had to be addressed.  "Usman's a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," he said.   "In his book, Uzzie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket."   Cummins added, though, that he would not be taking legal action against Khawaja over the allegations in the book.  "I did get advised this week that some of the things that've been said are probably defamatory, but I won't be doing that," Cummins said.  "You've got to move on. It's been eight years. We're moving on. So you got to draw a line at some point."

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON: United States House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday (Nov 12) there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government.  Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development. Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

"The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China's access to the advanced technology.  "I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take." The Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Related:

Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions. Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.   Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defence authorisation Bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.  Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four Bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday.  The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.  The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips. Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26.  House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.  Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 12 : Coco Gauff rallied to beat Marta Kostyuk 6-4 7-5 at the WTA Finals on Thursday and now needs fellow American Jessica Pegula to lose in order to reach the semi-finals of the season-ending championships. After sealing the first set with a stab volley that sent fans leaping to their feet under sunny California desert skies, Gauff rallied from 1-5 down in the second, winning six games in a row to keep her hopes of a second WTA Finals title alive. "I was fully prepared to play a third set there," said Gauff, who needed treatment on her hip during the second set. Whether twice major champion Gauff advances to the semis or is eliminated now hinges on her friend and frequent doubles partner Pegula, who takes on Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova later on Thursday.

FAST

Nov 12 : The US Treasury bought Japanese yen in the July-to-September quarter, but the Federal Reserve did not intervene on its own in foreign exchange markets in the same period, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Thursday. The New York Fed's quarterly report on currency market operations detailed interventions executed on behalf of the Treasury this summer to stem a sharp weakening of the yen. The purchase was the first US yen-buying intervention since 1998, and the report shows Washington acted alongside Tokyo to support the Japanese currency. On July 30, press reports emerged that the New York Fed had requested "rate checks" on the dollar-yen rate. The New York Fed report said the checks were made "solely on behalf of the US Treasury," with the New York Fed acting as the government's fiscal agent. The yen rose 2.3 per cent against the dollar that day.

A Reuters photograph taken during a cabinet meeting at Camp David on July 31 showed a "to-do" list in which Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appeared to be weighing US purchases of $5 billion to $10 billion worth of Japanese yen. The New York Fed said it bought 79.4 billion yen ($497.37 million) in the spot market on July 31, selling euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund. The New York Fed made the purchase "to counter what the US Treasury viewed as disorderly moves in the Japanese yen," its report said. Japan's Ministry of Finance acted in coordination, intervening "in the amount of 15.4 trillion yen" during the quarter to counter what it saw as excessive volatility and disorderly yen moves, the New York Fed added. Bessent said on August 2 that the US "will not hesitate to participate in further joint intervention," while repeating calls for further interest rate hikes by the Bank of Japan. The yen recovered quickly. Between July 30 and August 3, the dollar-yen rate fell "from around 164 yen per dollar to around 155 yen per dollar," the report said. The yen has since weakened. Japan's top currency diplomat, Atsushi Mimura, warned on Thursday that it was "too early to forget" this summer's intervention as the yen moved back toward 160 per dollar, its weakest level since September. Analysts at Mizuho Securities flagged the risk of Japanese intervention, saying the dollar was likely to keep rising against the yen, supported by resilience in the US economy and persistently high inflation driven by strong AI investment. Some Bank of Japan policymakers called in October for speeding up rate hikes, arguing that underlying inflation has reached the central bank's 2 per cent target. Their remarks strengthen the case for near-term tightening. A majority of economists in a Reuters poll expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent in December, extending the faster pace after increases in June and September. ($1 = 159.6400 yen)

US stocks a tap away: How Indian trading apps are changing investment habits

Major Indian stockbroking apps began making it easier for retail investors to buy US stocks last month. Experts tell CNA the move could reshape investment habits as Indians seek global opportunities, but warn of risks and potential implications for domestic markets.

FAST

BENGALURU: For  eight years, Bengaluru - based recruitment professional Jishnu Banerjee has invested in Indian stocks through online brokerage Zerodha. Now, the 40 - year - old is considering adding  shares in companies  based in the United States such as Apple and Meta to his portfolio. “It's good to have the option to diversify. It shouldn't matter whether the Indian market or the US market is doing better. I would want to diversify regardless,” he said.

Bengaluru-based recruitment professional Jishnu Banerjee, 40, is considering investing in US stocks through Zerodha to diversify his portfolio beyond Indian markets. (Photo: Jishnu Banerjee)

His interest comes as some of India's biggest stockbrokers make it easier for millions of existing customers to invest in US companies.

Three major Indian stockbrokers - Groww, Zerodha and Angel One - began rolling out services allowing customers to invest in US stocks in October.  Previously, Indian investors typically had to use specialist platforms to buy US stocks, with overseas money transfers often involving extra fees and delays.  The new services - introduced after Indian regulatory reforms in 2025 eased access to overseas markets - allow customers to invest through familiar apps, although currency-conversion costs and international transfer requirements remain. The growing interest in US stocks comes as Indian equities lag behind Wall Street, with India's benchmark Nifty 50 index falling nearly 12 per cent in the first ten months of 2026, while the US S&P 500 gained about 11 per cent.  Together, Groww and Zerodha accounted for nearly 44 per cent of active retail  user accounts on India's National Stock Exchange in September.  Harsh Jain, Groww’s co-founder and chief operating officer, told CNA that the launch reflected growing interest among Indian retail investors in global industries, including artificial intelligence, semiconductors, robotics and electric vehicles. He said American technology giants were among the most popular investments  Industry experts told CNA easier access could shift Indian savings overseas, potentially diverting money from domestic markets while exposing inexperienced investors to new risks. WHY INDIANS ARE LOOKING OVERSEAS The growing attraction of  US stocks reflects a shift in how Indian investors view opportunities beyond their home market. Until around 2024, when Indian equities were outperforming many overseas markets, investors largely sought international exposure to diversify their portfolios rather than earn higher returns, said Vishal Dhawan, founder of Mumbai-based wealth advisory firm Plan Ahead. “If you want high returns, you come to India. If you want diversification, you go overseas,” he said, describing the prevailing mindset at the time. But India's relative market underperformance since then, a weakening rupee and the boom in  US-based artificial intelligence companies have changed that calculation, he said. Dhawan said his firm had long advised many clients to keep around 20 per cent of their investments in overseas markets, spreading their money beyond Indian stocks. Previously, some questioned whether that allocation was dragging down their overall returns because Indian equities were performing better. Now, with overseas markets delivering stronger returns, some are asking whether 20  per cent is enough, he said. India's relatively limited exposure to AI-linked companies has also weighed on its stock market this year, Reuters reported on  Nov 4 , highlighting a gap that investors seeking to participate in the global AI boom may look overseas to fill.

More than half of investors who bought US securities through Groww have purchased at least one AI, big-tech or semiconductor stock, according to data shared by the company. “Some of the most popular US stocks include  Nvidia , SpaceX, Apple,  Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Micron, Tesla and Netflix,” said  Jain of Groww . He added that funds tracking major US stock indices, including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100, were also among the most popular investments. The appeal is also extending beyond affluent investors, according to  Ashish Kashyap, founder of investment platform INDmoney. The company said the median first international investment on its platform was US$150, while systematic investment plans (SIPs) - which enable regular investments in smaller amounts in global stocks - nearly doubled between September 2025 and September 2026.

Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City on Nov 10, 2026. (Photo: Angela Weiss/AFP)

“An investor may initially come to INDmoney to buy Nvidia, Google or Apple, but increasingly recognises the importance of building a diversified international portfolio rather than concentrating investments in a handful of companies, sectors or geographies,” Kashyap said. COULD INDIAN MARKETS LOSE OUT? The growing interest in overseas stocks comes at a time when foreign investors have been pulling money out of India's equity markets. Foreign  institutional investors pulled out a net 2.95 trillion  Indian rupees (about US$31 billion) from the  country’s stock markets in the first ten months of 2026, according to  a Press Trust of India report . Meanwhile, Indian residents invested US$2.61 billion in overseas stocks and debt instruments between January and August, up 86 per cent from a year earlier, according to  data from India’s central bank . The increase points to growing interest in foreign investments among Indians, even before major domestic brokerages launched their latest US stock investing services in October. Specialist platforms Vested and INDmoney have offered US stocks since 2019 and 2020 respectively, but the latest rollouts make overseas investing accessible through familiar brokerage apps. Groww itself offered US stocks in 2020 but halted new purchases in February 2024, citing transfer difficulties, high withdrawal fees and settlement delays. Investment platforms Groww and INDmoney said overseas investing is unlikely to replace domestic investments, with Kashyap suggesting it is “increasingly attracting incremental household savings” rather than diverting money from Indian equities. Customers typically start with less than 3 per cent of their portfolios invested overseas, raising that share to 7 to 10 per cent within eight to 12 months, according to INDmoney. However, wealth adviser Dhawan expects India's historically strong preference for domestic investments to gradually diminish as more investors diversify internationally. He said familiar brokerage platforms such as Groww and Zerodha could accelerate that shift by making investors more comfortable buying overseas shares. Nevertheless,  appetite for domestic investments remains strong.  For instance, telecom and digital services company Jio Platforms made its stock market debut on Oct 28 after raising about US$3.2 billion in India's largest-ever initial public offering (IPO). Its retail portion was oversubscribed 2.72 times, according to exchange data.

Indian billionaire and Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani (C) and his wife Nita Ambani (2L) with their children and Jio Platforms board members Isha Ambani (L), Akash Ambani (2R) and Anant Ambani at Jio's IPO listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange in Mumbai on Oct 28, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Indranil Mukherjee)

Growing overseas capital flows have also drawn regulatory scrutiny, with Bloomberg reporting on Oct 20 that India's central bank had stepped up checks on large overseas investments amid concerns over a weakening rupee. However, this is currently directed at companies, rather than individual retail investors.  THE RISKS OF CHASING WALL STREET Experts who spoke to CNA warned that easier access to  the US stock market could expose inexperienced Indian investors to unfamiliar risks, particularly if they are drawn to technology companies after their strong market performance. The risks were highlighted by a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks on Nov 5, which wiped about US$2.5 trillion off the Nasdaq-100's market value amid fears of tighter AI regulation and concerns over lofty valuations.  Nvidia shares had fallen nearly 29 per cent from their record high on Oct 6 by Nov 11, highlighting the risks for investors hoping to profit from the technology boom. Dhawan said investors might fall for “recency bias”, where they chase stocks that have recently delivered strong returns without considering whether those gains can continue. He said the social appeal of owning shares in famous companies such as Google or Amazon could also influence younger investors, even when they have limited understanding of the businesses. But Banerjee does not expect investing in familiar American companies to require much additional guidance. He said he would approach buying US shares much like investing in Indian stocks and did not expect brokerage platforms to provide extensive education for straightforward investments. Beyond market volatility, overseas investing brings complications that Indian investors may not encounter when buying domestic shares, Dhawan said.

Ashish Kashyap, founder of investment platform INDmoney (Photo: Ashish Kashyap)

For example, US estate taxes could apply to American shares owned by an Indian investor if they die, potentially reducing what their family inherits.  Dividends paid to shareholders may also be taxed in the US before investors receive them. Indian investors must also declare certain overseas holdings in their tax returns and account for currency-conversion fees and international money-transfer charges,  Dhawan said . These additional costs could eat into investment returns, particularly for those investing small amounts or trading frequently. Dhawan warned that the convenience of buying  US shares should not obscure the additional responsibilities that come with investing in another country. “Investors who fail to understand those obligations could end up creating problems for  themselves that they don't even understand,” he said.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid deepening scandal, leaving AI chip giant at crossroads

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO. Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, will not remain on the board.

FAST

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (Nov 12) after revelations of two extramarital affairs , including one involving a suspected Chinese spy , plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump. The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment. Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick's future. Earlier in the day, a White House official said US President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position." Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly US$6 trillion. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago. Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure. Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each. Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair. "The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18. Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation. REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products. "The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself." Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. Trump had urged Huang to fight for his job in a call on Tuesday, the New York Times reported. On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang", noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China. HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips. Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Related:

Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in Megaspeed probe: MHA

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said. Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

Source: Reuters/sz/fs
